newsitem.title: INDIA: India state plans bond issue for Enron stake.
newsitem.headline: India state plans bond issue for Enron stake.

text.p: India's western Maharashtra state said on Tuesday it plans a six-billion-rupee bond issue to finance the purchase of a 30 percent equity stake in a 2,450 MW power plant being built by the U.S.'s Enron Corp.
"We will raise six billion rupees through a private placement of bonds," Chief Minister Manohar Joshi told reporters following a weekly cabinet meeting.
"The state government has given the MSEB approval to take 30 percent equity in the Dabhol power project," Joshi said.

The state electricity board, MSEB, is the principal customer for the power generated by a $2.3-billion plant Enron is building in Maharashtra after India opened the sector to foreign investors as part of economic reforms that began in 1991.
Joshi said the cost of the equity stake would range between 4.7 billion rupees and 7.3 billion rupees, as he was unsure if the shares would be sold at a premium.
The bulk of this sum -- six billion rupees -- is to be raised through the privately-placed bonds.
Joshi said the state government would lend MSEB another 500 million rupees, 730 million rupees would come from state-run companies and agencies, and MSEB would raise 70 million.
But he gave no details about the date of the bond issue.
"Taking all the various factors into account, we are definitely hopeful that we will meet the target," Joshi said when asked about the bond issue's chances of success.
Under the terms of the state's agreement with Enron, it must exercise its option to purchase 30 percent of the equity by June 9, Joshi said.
"But we may ask for an extension," he added.
Enron holds 80 percent of the equity in the Dabhol Power Company, the local subsidiary building the project. The rest is split equally between Bechtel Group Inc and General Electric Capital Services.
The project's 740-MW first phase is scheduled to be completed by December 1998.
